title: Korean Bulgogi Rice Bowls
seoTitle: Korean Bulgogi Rice Bowls | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Sweet soy beef, pickled crunch
description: Sweet soy beef, pickled crunch. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Marinate sliced beef
steps.instruction: Toss thinly sliced ribeye with soy sauce, brown sugar, grated pear or apple, garlic, and sesame oil. Marinate 20 minutes while rice cooks.

steps.title: Cook short-grain rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice; cook 1:1.25 with water 15 minutes. Rest covered 10 minutes.

steps.title: Sear bulgogi in batches
steps.instruction: Heat a cast iron skillet until smoking. Sear beef in single layers 2–3 minutes per side until caramelized edges appear — do not crowd or meat steams instead of chars.

steps.title: Build bulgogi bowls
steps.instruction: Rice, seared beef, kimchi, and julienned cucumber. Korean Bulgogi Rice Bowls need that char on the beef — batch the skillet if the crew is hungry.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Set rice or grain in the first pan, main in the second, crunchy toppings last so textures stay distinct.
Put hot components closest to the crew, cold crunch at the far end of the line.
Line up Korean Bulgogi Rice Bowls on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sweet soy beef, pickled crunch. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
